question: What evidence supports the 2025 report of juvenile bull sharks caught around Lagyo in Hagonoy, and can it be assigned to the EMB-listed Hagonoy River?

sourceAccess.media: GMA and Manila Bulletin article text plus the GMA Public Affairs Dailymotion broadcast page and its rendered English transcript were reviewed on 2026-11-27. The video page was accessible; the underlying video was not downloaded, visually inspected, or audio-transcribed independently. The broadcast gives a tentative photo-based shark identification and renders the local name as Laguio, while the article spells it Lagyo. No media assets were retained and no reuse terms were verified.
sourceAccess.locality: The official Bulacan PFP and Provincial Government photo release were opened. The PFP lists Matimbo Mangrove Area (Lagyo) under Bulakan; the photo release identifies Hagonoy River along San Agustin. Neither source links the reported Lagyo/Laguio event location to that Hagonoy River reach.
sourceAccess.gbif: Read-only GBIF Occurrence API and Species API v1 requests returned HTTP 200 on 2026-11-27. Only query counts, selected name-match fields, URLs, and SHA-256 response hashes are recorded; no occurrence payloads were retained.
sourceAccess.terms: No media reuse terms or occurrence-level dataset licenses were verified. No article photograph or other image was copied.

mediaEvent.reportedEventDate: 2025-02 (GMA says the catch occurred in the preceding February; no day is given)

published.reportedPlace: a river section called Lagyo in Hagonoy, Bulacan
published.reportedCatch: three juvenile bull sharks reportedly caught in a fishing net
published.reportedIdentification: Animal expert Dr. Romulo Bernardo identified the animals as bull sharks in the report.
published.reportedDisposition: The fisher reportedly released them while they were weak and was unsure whether they survived.

published.reportedCatch: the same three juvenile sharks caught by fisher Rex Arceo
published.reportedDisposition: The article says they were released back into the river and uses a screengrab from the Dami Mong Alam, Kuya Kim report.

originatingBroadcast.reviewedMaterial: The page metadata and rendered English transcript were reviewed; video frames and Filipino audio were not independently inspected.

transcriptObservations.observation: The transcript says Rex's Hagonoy catch consisted of three juveniles and renders the expert's photo-based opinion as 'more likely a bull shark.' This is tentative reporting, not a specimen determination.

The transcript places the encounter in February and renders the local river name as 'Laguio'; GMA's written article spells the name 'Lagyo.' The audio and exact spelling were not independently checked.
The transcript reports that the fisher released the three sharks and was unsure whether they survived because they were weak.

mediaEvent.independence: The two articles and the GMA Public Affairs broadcast trace to the same reported catch. The broadcast is the originating media account, not an independent field survey or a separate specimen record; the Manila Bulletin identifies its image as a screengrab from that report.
mediaEvent.evidenceClass: dated broadcast and secondary-media catch lead with a tentative expert photo-based common-name opinion; not a museum voucher, retained specimen, genetic record, or independently inspected field survey.

reportedNames: Laguio (spelling in the Dailymotion-rendered English transcript; audio not independently checked)
Hagonoy River (Manila Bulletin's event label and the separate EMB/locality crosswalk name)

officialLocalityChecks.finding: The provincial plan's mangrove table lists 'Matimbo Mangrove Area (Lagyo)' under Bulakan, not Hagonoy. It is a distinct named mangrove locality, not evidence that the reported catch occurred there or that the label identifies a river reach.

A provincial photo release identifies a Hagonoy River dredging project along San Agustin, Hagonoy. It supplies no coordinates, reach geometry, or connection to the incident's reported Lagyo/Laguio locality.

waterbodyCrosswalk.decision: The article and broadcast associate the same event with the Hagonoy area, but the written article's 'Lagyo' and the broadcast page's rendered transcript 'Laguio' are not reconciled against the Filipino audio or an authoritative map. The provincial plan also uses 'Lagyo' for a mangrove locality in the separate municipality of Bulakan, while a different provincial source locates Hagonoy River along San Agustin; neither links the incident to that river reach. Preserve the spellings and media association as a candidate only; do not create a canonical alias or geometry.

taxonomy.basis: The broadcast transcript attributes a tentative photo-based opinion ('more likely a bull shark') to the expert. GBIF Backbone separately returned an exact accepted species-name match at confidence 97 for the typed candidate name Carcharhinus leucas. Neither source independently identifies the animals; the video and diagnostic images were not visually reviewed.
taxonomy.specimenIdentification: Not independently verified; no retained specimen, diagnostic photo review, tissue, or voucher was located in the reviewed sources.

gbifScreen.scope: Bounded exact text searches, not an exhaustive survey or absence assessment.

fishTaxonomy.name: Catalogue of Life Extended Release Actinopterygii

queries.label: CoL XR Actinopterygii; stateProvince=Bulacan and locality=Hagonoy
CoL XR Actinopterygii positive query-path control; waterBody=Laguna de Bay

bullSharkCandidate.nationalResultNote: The four returned GBIF rows were labeled Cebu City, Cebu, and Dapitan City, Zamboanga del Norte. Two rows share the same catalog number across FishBase and SEAOBIS and may represent a duplicate; no deduplication decision was made. No Hagonoy record was returned by the localized exact-text queries.

gbifScreen.interpretation: The Laguna de Bay control returned 22 under the same CoL XR fish filters, confirming that the Actinopterygii query path returned indexed records. Zero exact-text matches do not show that fish are absent, that no survey exists, or that Lagyo is not connected to Hagonoy River. GBIF search may miss unindexed names, alternate spellings, taxon treatments, and locality fields.

method.approach: Reviewed the GMA Public Affairs Dailymotion page and its rendered English transcript alongside two reports of the same media event; compared its reported local names with the official Bulacan PFP mangrove locality and the provincial Hagonoy River along San Agustin reference; checked the exact Carcharhinus leucas name against GBIF Backbone; queried GBIF exact locality/waterBody fields for the CoL XR Actinopterygii class and the candidate bull-shark taxon; included a positive Laguna de Bay query-path control.
method.limits: The broadcast page was opened but its video frames and Filipino audio were not independently inspected; the transcript is rendered in English and its 'Laguio' spelling may not reflect the spoken or official name. No underlying field documentation, diagnostic photo review, exact event date, coordinates, or specimen/voucher was located. GBIF zero exact-string counts are limited to the requested indexed fields and filters. The four national candidate records were not fully audited against their collection institutions.

nextActions: If a direct species determination is needed, obtain and review the original shark images/video with a qualified shark taxonomist; the broadcast transcript records only a tentative photo-based opinion.
Find an independent field, specimen, or collection record for the reported catch; do not treat the two articles as independent occurrence records.

Resolve the 'Lagyo'/'Laguio' spelling and whether the reported place names the same reach as the EMB Hagonoy River monitoring unit using checked Filipino audio and a source with an explicit station, map, or coordinates before adding a canonical alias or geometry.
Keep the report visible as a research lead, but do not publish a bull-shark river occurrence, fishing advice, or image from this media-only evidence.

sources.supports: GMA Integrated News' dated media account of three juvenile bull sharks reportedly caught at a river section called Lagyo in Hagonoy in February 2025, the fisher's release account, and the expert-reported common-name identification.

The originating GMA Public Affairs broadcast page and its rendered English transcript: three juvenile sharks reportedly caught and released, a tentative photo-based 'more likely a bull shark' opinion, and the transcript spelling 'Laguio'; no specimen, exact coordinates, or verified reach identity.
A second publication's account of the same three-shark catch, its Hagonoy River label, and its attribution of a screengrab to the same television report; not independent survey evidence.
The official provincial plan's separate Matimbo Mangrove Area (Lagyo) locality under Bulakan; used as a name-collision warning only, not a Hagonoy catch-location or river crosswalk.
The provincial source's Hagonoy River place reference along San Agustin; it does not identify a coordinate or connect the reported Lagyo/Laguio event reach.
The exact GBIF query terms, filters, HTTP statuses, result counts, response hashes, and the bounded interpretation of zero textual matches.
GBIF Backbone's exact accepted name match for the typed name Carcharhinus leucas; nomenclature only, not the identity of the reported animals.
